The user is in LMAgent mode. I need to output JSON-structured results without headings or Markdown formatting, based on the candidate's validated profile and the job offer text.

Let me analyze the match:

**Candidate Profile:**
- Léa Dubois, Data scientist junior, Bordeaux
- Master Data Science, Université de Bordeaux (current, started 2024-09)
- Available: February 2027, 6 months internship, Bordeaux, accepts remote

**Job Offer:**
- Stage de fin d'études — Data scientist (6 mois)
- Hélio Prévisions, Bordeaux (hybride)
- Starts février 2027, requires Python, SQL, séries temporelles, appreciates Power BI and Docker, professional English, last-year master student

Checking each requirement against her profile: Python and SQL both show up in her Banque Atlantique experience, time series work appears in her tramway prediction project with LightGBM, Power BI is also covered by the banking experience, and she matches the master's level requirement too.

She's based in Bordeaux and started her master in September 2024, so by February 2027 she'd indeed be in her final year. The six-month duration and C1 English both line up. Docker isn't mentioned anywhere in her profile though, so that's a gap. Dashboard creation and predictive modeling are both solidly covered through her Power BI and LightGBM time series work.

Overall this is a very strong match — all the must-haves are covered except Docker, so I'd put the score around 88/100. I have everything I need to produce the full output: score, strengths with evidence, gaps, a French cover letter since that's the offer's language, and CV adjustments. No clarifying questions are needed since motivation, company context, start date, and hiring manager name are all already available. I'll draft the cover letter under 300 words, dated from Bordeaux and addressed to M. Julien Roche, keeping it as plain text with no headings or Markdown per LMAgent mode requirements.

I'm drafting the letter addressed to M. Julien Roche, introducing myself as a second-year Master's student in Data Science seeking a six-month internship, and linking my tramway ridership forecasting project with gradient boosting to the role's requirements.

I'm adding my experience at Banque Atlantique automating SQL data extraction and building Power BI dashboards used by 40 advisors, drawing a parallel to the SQL reliability and dashboard tasks mentioned in the job posting, then closing with my availability starting February 2027.

Now I'm drafting the sign-off with my contact details, and shifting to reviewing the CV itself — thinking about whether to reposition the tramway frequentation forecasting project (using LightGBM on time series data) to better highlight its relevance to the role's forecasting needs.

I'm also checking the skills section: Docker isn't listed, but since she doesn't actually have that skill I shouldn't suggest adding it as "learning." I'm weighing whether to retitle the headline to emphasize "prévision" and "séries temporelles" more directly, and considering reordering the experience section to lead with the most relevant project.

5. Projet tramway: ajouter un bullet sur la méthodologie (sourcing des données open data, feature engineering pour les patterns horaires) pour démontrer le pipeline complet pertinent pour la prévision de consommation énergétique. Je passe maintenant à la mise en forme finale en JSON.
